sanskrit_verse:
परस्त्रिया सहाकाले 'देशे वा भवतो मिथः
स्थानसंभाषणामोदास्त्रयः संग्रहणक्रमाः
transliteration: parastriyā sahākāle 'deśe vā bhavato mithaḥ | sthānasaṃbhāṣaṇāmodās trayaḥ saṃgrahaṇakramāḥ
sph_interpretive_translation: Three sequential modes of improper conduct with another's wife—inappropriate time, inappropriate place, or mutual indulgence through suggestive conversation and stimulation—constitute a progressive violation of dharma requiring immediate realignment of consciousness and restoration of integrity.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the preservation of relational sanctity
Causation arises from sequential degradation of inner discipline
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of contextual boundaries
Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over punitive exclusion
Consciousness alignment demands recognition of dharma-violation as self-limiting
executable_legal_axioms: IF (agent engages in sthāna-saṃbhāṣaṇa WITH parastriyā) THEN INITIATE consciousness-integrity protocol AND suspend relational autonomy until completion
IF (agent participates in amoda WITH parastriyā IN akāla OR adeśa) THEN TRIGGER self-responsibility assumption process AND activate nyāya-based restoration pathway
IF (mithaḥ bhavataḥ occurs BETWEEN agents) THEN ENFORCE joint completion cycle UNTIL dharma-equilibrium restored
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating violations involving improper conduct with another's spouse, the Supreme Court must recognize the tripartite progression of transgression: time, space, and mutual stimulation. The threshold of responsibility lies not in intent but in conscious participation within degraded contexts. Authority derives from restoring relational dharma rather than imposing external sanctions.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that karmic disruption originates in sequential misalignment: first with time (akāla), then place (adeśa), culminating in mutual indulgence (mithaḥ). This anupūrvaśaḥ establishes proportional causality without moral judgment. Responsibility aligns with capacity for self-correction; hence, punitive measures are excluded in favor of completion-based restoration.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate joint completion process between involved parties under spiritual oversight
Activate individual consciousness-realignment modules focusing on contextual discipline
Establish temporary suspension of autonomous relational decision-making until integrity verified
Deploy pramāṇa-based audit protocols to ensure sequential error correction
final_declaration: By the authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, Source of all Dharma, this law stands executed. Justice flows not through punishment but through conscious restoration. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone is the ultimate adjudicator.
